title: RESCUE: Is This Alarm Worth Acting On? Counterfactual Evaluation of VLA Runtime Monitors
abstract: arXiv:2610.13516v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Runtime failure monitors for robot policies are typically evaluated by how accurately they distinguish failed from successful executions. Yet an accurate alarm may arrive too late for recovery, while an unnecessary intervention may disrupt an execution that would otherwise succeed. We introduce RESCUE, a counterfactual framework for evaluating whether a monitor's alarms enable useful interventions. By restoring simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints, RESCUE compares alternative actions, identifies the latest checkpoint satisfying a specified recovery criterion, and evaluates whether acting on alarms reduces expected task-completion cost. We evaluate RESCUE with OpenVLA-OFT and $\pi_{0.5}$ over LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Plus using 128,340 counterfactual branches. translated_title: RESCUE：这个警报值得采取行动吗？VLA运行时监控器的反事实评估
translated_abstract: 机器人策略的运行时故障监控器通常根据其区分失败执行与成功执行的准确性来评估。然而，一个准确的警报可能到达得太晚而无法进行恢复，而不必要的干预可能会破坏原本会成功的执行。我们提出了RESCUE，一个用于评估监控器的警报是否能够实现有效干预的反事实框架。通过在执行检查点处恢复模拟器和策略状态，RESCUE比较替代动作，识别满足指定恢复标准的最新检查点，并评估根据警报采取行动是否能降低预期的任务完成成本。我们使用128,340个反事实分支，在LIBERO-Spatial和LIBERO-Plus数据集上结合OpenVLA-OFT和π0.5对RESCUE进行了评估。可恢复性取决于状态-干预对，而不仅仅取决于机器人状态本身：在τ=0.5时，66个OpenVLA-OFT/LIBERO-Plus失败案例中有14个包含可恢复的情形（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出了RESCUE反事实评估框架，通过在执行检查点恢复模拟器和策略状态来评估VLA运行时监控器的警报是否能带来有效干预，并发现可恢复性取决于状态-干预对而非仅取决于机器人状态本身。
en_tdlr: RESCUE is a counterfactual framework that evaluates whether VLA runtime monitor alarms enable useful interventions by restoring simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints, revealing that recoverability depends on the state-intervention pair rather than robot state alone.
